newsitem.title: USA: PanCanadian to acquire CS Resources.
newsitem.headline: PanCanadian to acquire CS Resources.

text.p: PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd said early Wednesday it has an agreement to acquire CS Resources Ltd for $16 per share plus the assumption of $56 million of debt, for a total purchase price of $521 million.
The deal has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies and an acquisition agreement has been signed.
"This acquisition will combine the strengths of two of Canada's leading heavy oil producers,'' PanCanadian President and Chief Executive David Tuer said in a statement.
"We believe that PanCanadian's offer price will be highly attractive to our shareholders and is certainly a fair price,'' CS Resources Chairman and Chief Executive Dennis Sharp said in a statement.

As part of the agreement, CS Resources will pay PanCanadian a non-completion fee of 3 percent in certain circumstances. In addition, CS Resources has granted PanCanadian the right of first refusal to match any subsequent bids. CS Resources has also agreed not to solicit other transaction proposals, it said.

The offer represents a 41.6 per cent premium on the closing price of CS Resources' shares on The Toronto Stock Exchange on June 5, the day before Gulf Canada Resources Ltd announced it planned to bid for CS Resources, the companies said.
The PanCanadian offer is also a 17 per cent premium to the value of Gulf Canada's cash and share offer based on Gulf's closing price on June 17, they said.
The offer is conditional upon 66 2/3 per cent of CS Resources' outstanding shares being tendered.
PanCanadian does not currently own any CS Resources shares. PanCanadian said it will pay for the purchase from existing cash balances.
CS Resources reported proved and one-half probable crude oil reserves of 132 million barrels and 44 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
Based on first quarter reports, the combined daily production of the new PanCanadian would be about 155,000 barrels of oil and liquids and 738 million cubic feet of natural gas, the company said.
After the transaction closes, CS Resources will become the heavy oil arm of PanCanadian.
